code:

print(a)
print(b)
ms: Both print [99, 2, 3] (2) — b = a does NOT copy the list; both names point at the SAME list in memory (1), so changing it through either name shows through both (1). To copy for real: b = a[:] or list(a). A famous trap — worth remembering even beyond the exam.

q:
Write a complete Python program for a mini class-record system.

Requirements: store `names = ["Ada", "Ben", "Cai", "Dee"]` and `marks = [72, 45, 88, 61]` as parallel lists; print each pupil's name with their mark; then print the class average to 1 decimal place; finally print the name of the top-scoring pupil. (6)
ms: Parallel lists assigned (1); paired printing via one index loop — names[i], marks[i] (1); total accumulated and average = total / len(marks) (1); rounded with round(avg, 1) → 66.5 (1); find-max tracking the INDEX of the best mark (1); top name printed via that index → Cai (1).
msCode:
names = ["Ada", "Ben", "Cai", "Dee"]
marks = [72, 45, 88, 61]
total = 0
for i in range(len(names)):
    print(names[i], marks[i])
    total = total + marks[i]
avg = total / len(marks)
print(round(avg, 1))
best = 0
for i in range(len(marks)):
    if marks[i] > marks[best]:
        best = i
print(names[best])
